\title{Medora: A bilingual, consent-gated healthcare management and consultation
platform with assistive AI for Bangladesh}

\author{Sarwad Hasan Siddiqui}
\author{Adiba Tahsin}
\author{Kazi Saeed Alam\corref{cor1}}
\ead{saeed.alam@cse.kuet.ac.bd}
\cortext[cor1]{Corresponding author.}
\address{Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Khulna University of Engineering \& Technology, Khulna 9203, Bangladesh}

\begin{abstract}
Medora joins bilingual English/Bengali patient-held records and appointment coordination
to twenty-one assistive-AI endpoints in an installable progressive web application.
External calls require purpose-specific revocable grants and configured redaction and
pseudonymisation, which reduce exposure without establishing anonymity. Navigation uses
a fixed role-scoped registry without administrative routes; summaries cite backend-supplied
records. Routing, consent and red-flag detection are deterministic. The historical
Bangladesh reference contains 7{,}389 drugs and 67{,}001 brands; a separately attributed
revision rebuild is prepared. Evaluation documents software behaviour through privacy,
navigation, summary and booking fixtures. Medora supports research workflows; clinical
effectiveness is outside this evaluation.
\end{abstract}

\begin{keyword}
digital health \sep assistive AI \sep consent-gated processing \sep
medicine reference data \sep deterministic intent routing \sep bilingual software
\end{keyword}
\end{frontmatter}

\section{Motivation and significance}

Medora provides researchers and educators with a bilingual environment for studying
patient-held workflows, consent, assistive-AI containment and booking concurrency.

Studies describe uneven Bangladesh eHealth implementation and clinician concerns about
electronic-record adoption~\cite{ahmed2014,khan2012}. Medora addresses these concerns
through inspectable bilingual workflows in a research setting.

The medicine reference addresses nationally scoped terminology services such as RxNorm,
which omit Bangladesh~\cite{rxnorm}. Its revision builder inventories five sources,
consolidating four into a normalized three-table identity reference.

The containment pattern checks consent before external calls, resolves navigation through
a fixed registry, and attaches summary sources after schema validation
(Table~\ref{tab:components}).

OpenMRS, Bahmni and GNU Health cover wider institution-facing medical-record, hospital,
laboratory and Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) capabilities
~\cite{openmrs,bahmni,gnuhealth}. Medora links patient-held records and booking to an
inspectable assistive-AI layer (Table~\ref{tab:related-work}); these systems are complements,
not performance baselines.

Clinical-summary studies assess correctness and completeness beyond fluency, while clinician--AI trials show task- and workflow-dependent effects~\cite{shing2021,tracsum,zhang2024clinicalsummary,goh2025gpt4assistance}. Bangla-HealthNER documents informal, code-mixed Bengali health text~\cite{khan2023banglahealthner}. Re-identification and prompt-injection studies show why redaction and model instructions alone cannot contain risk~\cite{campion2025diri,yang2025adversarial}; symptom-checker studies find variable diagnostic and urgency performance~\cite{wallace2022}. Medora contributes an integration of consent checks, bounded routing, and reviewable drafts. It offers candidates rather than diagnosis and makes no clinical-performance claim.

\section{Software description}

\subsection{Software architecture}

Medora is a Next.js web client, a FastAPI core API, a separate FastAPI OCR service, and
PostgreSQL (Fig.~\ref{fig:trust}). Authentication identifies the actor. Backend role,
ownership, care-relationship, appointment-state, and consent checks authorize each
operation, and frontend visibility is only a usability aid.

Authorization is enforced at both API and database boundaries. The release restricts
anonymous direct-data access, enables row-level security and exposes a trigger-maintained
change feed. Access-denial tests verify that direct requests cannot bypass application
permissions.

\begin{figure}[!h]
\centering\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{\input{figures-src/trust_boundary.tex}}
\caption{Deployment and trust boundaries. Local speech recognition and OCR cross no
external boundary. Hosted text models, Vapi live audio, and Azure OCR are separate
recipients with separate grants.}
\label{fig:trust}
\end{figure}

Processing is deny-by-default (Fig.~\ref{fig:consent}). Persisted grants record subject,
recipient, purpose, scopes, policy version, validity, grant/revocation times and audit
metadata. Sharing controls expose this choice. Missing, expired, revoked or wrong-scope
grants produce typed denials and local alternatives where available. Revocation blocks
future processing, not past disclosure; local mode never falls back to cloud services.

Medora uses private JSON/REST contracts and human-readable PDF output. It neither provides
structured EHR import/export nor claims FHIR or IHE conformance. The grant maps
conceptually to FHIR Consent subject, grantee, purpose, period, scoped data, and provisions;
the patient-visible read log is analogous to Provenance~\cite{fhirconsent}. No FHIR profile,
terminology binding, consent exchange, or IHE PCF transaction has been implemented or
tested~\cite{ihepcf}. This is an adapter boundary, not interoperability evidence.

For an EU deployment, health data remain special-category personal data and
pseudonymisation does not remove controller obligations; lawful basis, an Article 9
condition, processor/transfer/retention arrangements, data-subject workflows, and likely a
DPIA require deployment-specific legal review~\cite{gdpr}. Medora makes no GDPR compliance
claim. MDR classification depends on intended purpose and use; clinical-investigation use
has separate obligations. German AMG provisions concern medicinal-product trials, which
Medora is not designed or assessed to conduct~\cite{mdr,amg}.

\begin{figure}[!h]
\centering\resizebox{\textwidth}{!}{\input{figures-src/consent_flow.tex}}
\caption{Consent-aware processing. Purpose and provider are checked before any external
call; outputs stay non-authoritative drafts.}
\label{fig:consent}
\end{figure}

\subsection{Software functionalities}

\textbf{Medicine reference.} Search, medication linking, prescription composition and
OCR matching share one identity. \texttt{drugs} keys immutable identities on generic,
strength and form; \texttt{brands} maps commercial names onto them;
\texttt{medicine\_search\_index} supports trigram lookup (Table~\ref{tab:corpus}).
The revision uses four of five inventoried sources, excluding Indian indication text.
Dosage logic, interaction checking and effectiveness ranking are non-goals.

\begin{table}[!h]
\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lr@{}}
\toprule
Artifact & Count \\
\midrule
Consolidated source rows & 71{,}795 \\
Canonical drugs (generic $\times$ strength $\times$ form) & 7{,}389 \\
Brand entries & 67{,}001 \\
Search-index terms & 74{,}390 \\
Distinct generic names & 5{,}242 \\
Distinct brand names & 52{,}117 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Historical application snapshot, retained separately from the revision rebuild.
Counts describe existing runtime observations, not market completeness or reproduction
of the undocumented original build.}
\label{tab:corpus}
\end{table}

The candidate has 46{,}614 records, 6{,}153 drug identities and 52{,}767 projected search
terms. Each row links hashed source files, record numbers, original fields and
transformations. Conservative normalization preserves identities; exact duplicates are
merged and contradictory mappings/ambiguous strengths quarantined. Manifests record
independent rebuilds and source-link checks, not clinical correctness or regulatory
currency. Historical measurements and the shared database remain unchanged.

\textbf{Assistive-AI layer.} Twenty-one endpoints share one pipeline
(Tables~\ref{tab:ai-surface},~\ref{tab:components}). An orchestrator selects Groq, Gemini,
Cerebras or a deterministic mock, recursively sanitizes input, calls under a random
correlation identifier, validates Pydantic output and records latency/provider metadata.
Raw prompts, transcripts and findings are not logged by default; malformed responses
raise rather than degrade to unvalidated prose.

Three guards run before the orchestrator. A consent guard returns the permitted categories,
filters the payload, and prepends a restriction notice when anything was removed, so the
model knows it is reasoning over a partial record. A redaction stage targets emails,
telephone numbers, addresses, national and passport identifiers, account numbers, and dates
in both scripts. The frozen production-path fixture report measures 75.5\% recall, with 23 of 94 identifier
spans retained. External processing therefore remains consent-gated and pseudonymised:
residual identifier text may reach an authorized provider. A pseudonymiser replaces the stable subject header,
and audit records use correlation metadata rather than raw prompts by default. Doctor reads
of a patient record also require a care relationship and go to a patient-visible audit.

Chorui implements this pattern for in-app navigation (Fig.~\ref{fig:chorui}). An utterance is normalized to a canonical intent, then resolved
against an immutable tuple of typed registry entries binding intent and role scope to a
route, its required parameters, and a fallback. The registry holds 24 entries over 23
canonical intents, 11 patient-scoped and 11 doctor-scoped with 2 shared. Administrative
routes are never registered, and missing parameters produce a clarification, not a guess.
Destinations are fixed at build time and auditable from one file, unlike free-form tool
selection where the prompt is the only control.

\begin{figure}[!h]
\centering\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures-src/chorui_architecture.pdf}
\caption{Chorui request path. Intent normalization and registry resolution are
deterministic. The model contributes phrasing, not the set of reachable destinations.}
\label{fig:chorui}
\end{figure}

Summaries for patients, prescribers, and prescription histories are read-only. The backend
attaches source references after schema validation, so an item can cite only a record the
request supplied, and a request carrying no source record returns a not-found item instead
of model prose. Record timestamps are stripped before the prompt leaves the deployment, so
the model cannot reason about temporal order. A clinician-verification warning stays visible
and nothing writes back automatically.

Local faster-whisper transcription is preloaded at startup and crosses no external
boundary~\cite{whisper}; only the structuring step uses a hosted model. Vapi live audio is a
separate external recipient needing its own grant at capture and again when callbacks are
processed, and local mode never escalates to it.

\textbf{Reviewable outputs.} Summaries remain read-only drafts; prescription suggestions
pre-fill fields for a prescriber to edit and sign. Specialty search places candidates
alongside manual browsing. Recognised prescription
images return a draft flagged \texttt{authoritative\_writeback=false} that a person verifies
row by row. A patient's later action is \texttt{receipt\_acknowledged} or
\texttt{discrepancy\_reported}, neither of which says a medicine is appropriate.

\textbf{Installable patient client.} The patient interface is a progressive web
application: a manifest declaring standalone display and maskable icons installs it to a
phone home screen, and the browser suite asserts the service worker activates and controls
the page. Caching is scoped, not general. Only versioned static and public resources are
cached, health writes never background-synchronize, and logout clears caches, IndexedDB,
session and sensitive local storage.

\textbf{Appointment transaction and delivery.} Creating an appointment requires an
\texttt{Idempotency-Key}. The backend locks the key and slot, validates availability, and
writes the appointment, idempotency result, audit record, and outbox event in one
transaction, with a uniqueness constraint as the last defense against duplicate active
slots. Only committed outbox events are published, so consistency ends at commit and
propagation is a later event measured separately. After a reconnect, clients re-query
PostgreSQL, which stays authoritative. A background dispatcher turns medication and
appointment reminders into in-app notifications and email; web push is optional and stays
off unless VAPID keys are configured.

\subsection{Evaluation and reproducibility}

Evaluation examines privacy processing, navigation, summary source references and booking
concurrency using defined correctness criteria. Mock and recorded-provider results are
reported separately.

The privacy suite is a hand-authored synthetic bilingual corpus covering the identifier
groups in Table~\ref{tab:privacy-span-results} together with spacing and misspelling
variants, obfuscated formats, over-redaction controls, consent state, and prompt injection.
It measures the production call path with no known identifiers supplied to the redactor.
The frozen v1.0.2 report records 71 true positives, 4 false positives, and 23 false negatives
over 94 expected spans (94.7\% precision, 75.5\% recall, and 3.2\% false redaction).
These figures describe the frozen fixtures rather than an independently held-out
population or subsequent source changes. Retained identifiers include personal/clinician
names in prose, month-name dates and obfuscated contacts. The archived results document
these cases; pseudonymisation and consent remain necessary at the provider boundary.

Navigation fixtures score the recorded-provider and deterministic-mock paths separately
against the classifier the request path itself uses. The deterministic emergency screen has
TP=7, FN=0, FP=5, and TN=18; Table~\ref{tab:navigation-emergency-results} reports
sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value with
two-sided 95\% Wilson intervals. Uncertainty is a flag beside candidates rather than a fourth
exclusive class, and every path asserts that manual browsing stays available. The screen
also matches some negated, third-person, and historical mentions. These clinician-reviewed
fixtures are preliminary software checks, not clinical triage accuracy.
Summary fixtures run the summarizer end to end under the mock provider and assert
that no item cites a record the backend did not supply, that an empty request produces a
not-found item, and that malformed output raises instead of degrading.

The evaluation treats consent, redaction, route allowlisting and schema checks as software
invariants. An LLM-only/deterministic-only/hybrid ablation and comparative clinical-output
evaluation are outside its scope.

Booking contention comprised 30 fresh-slot trials per level (2, 10, 50 requests), plus one
excluded warm-up. Each required one persisted winner, expected conflicts, idempotent replay,
mismatched-key rejection, and outbox processing. Table~\ref{tab:booking-results} reports n
and nearest-rank p50/p95/p99 for transaction and outbox latency. Environment, raw observations,
and 95\% trial-cluster bootstrap intervals are archived. In-process ASGI timings are not
deployed-capacity estimates.

\IfFileExists{generated/safety_results.tex}{\input{generated/safety_results.tex}}{}
\IfFileExists{generated/booking_results.tex}{\input{generated/booking_results.tex}}{}

The provider manifest records model/interface, region, generation settings, timeout,
retries, fallback, execution date, retention and paid-service assumptions. Recorded-provider
fixtures use archived outputs; other adapters are unevaluated. Code Ocean runs deterministic
fixture checks and regenerates tables from frozen reports, not host-specific timings.
Installation commands, checksums, raw outputs and table-generation instructions accompany
the archive.
%

\textbf{Experimental prescription OCR.} Region detection, local/cloud recognition, dosage
grammar, Bengali numeral normalization and catalog matching form a review-gated pipeline
~\cite{du2020,prescriptionocr}. Exploratory handwritten-prescription use required substantial
manual correction: cursive text and partial tokens produced incorrect or empty matches.
Users must verify every extracted row before saving it. This experimental feature has no
reported task-accuracy benchmark; review gating addresses automatic writeback rather than
establishing clinical reliability.

The YOLO26s model card records the authors' Roboflow v2 attribution, corrected Colab
recipe, artifact checksums and inspected metadata. PT settings agree with the notebook,
and all 204 matched named ONNX tensors agree exactly after fusion. This verifies current
parameter correspondence. Historical dataset linkage, differing validation logs and
runtime-output differences are documented separately; the check does not measure held-out
accuracy or full prediction equivalence. Approved weight distribution includes AGPL-3.0
corresponding source, while prescription images remain private.

\section{Illustrative examples}

The patient dashboard displays stored-record coverage, $100n/4$, where $n$ is the number
of measurement groups with finite readings in today's UTC window up to the snapshot.
Groups comprise steps, sleep, heart rate and blood pressure (requiring both components).
The adjacent panel lists their presence; the disclosure explains inputs and timestamps.
Unavailable responses are distinct from zero. Coverage describes data presence rather
than health or measurement quality and does not recommend recording all four groups.

\textit{Example workflow.} A doctor with a valid \texttt{specialty\_navigation} grant sends
a redacted request and receives an uncertain specialty candidate beside manual browsing;
diagnosis and prescription requests are refused. A request for an admin route yields no
destination because the registry contains none. A summary request with laboratory data
withheld drops that category, carries a restriction notice, and records the read in the
patient-visible audit table.

\section{Impact}

Medora provides an inspectable environment for research on purpose-specific consent,
bilingual interaction, source traceability and concurrent booking. Researchers can reuse
the medicine builder, deterministic mock and role-scoped registry, or test how consent
and record availability affect assistant workflows. Transaction and outbox measurements
separate database consistency from notification delivery.

The reported evidence covers software fixtures and one booking topology. Three AI endpoint
groups have task-level fixture checks; six remain documented capabilities. Application-specific
validation is needed for summary faithfulness, handwritten OCR, exhaustive identifier/red-flag
coverage and current medicine registration. Provider behaviour, cost and retention also depend
on deployment. Clinical trials, regulatory assessment and penetration testing are outside
the reported evaluation.

\section{Conclusions}

Medora integrates bilingual patient-held records, transactional booking and consent-gated
assistive AI~\cite{medorasw}. Its reusable medicine builder and role-scoped workflow provide
a concrete basis for software research. The accompanying fixtures and source-linked artifacts
make the evaluated behaviour inspectable, while human review governs clinical drafts.

\section*{Ethics and data availability}
\label{sec:ethics}

Project-authored source retains its MIT notices; the optional combined detector
distribution uses AGPL-3.0 with corresponding source and preserved notices. Synthetic
fixtures and aggregate results use CC BY 4.0. The interface figures come from a non-production demonstration
deployment: the patient record belongs to a consenting author and the clinician entries are
test accounts.

The revision medicine build inventories five sources, using four for identity fields,
including Mendeley Data V1 under CC BY 4.0~\cite{bdmeds}. It excludes indication prose
and preserves row-level attribution and changes. The authors select multi-source public
distribution after documenting its source permissions; platform labels alone are not
treated as upstream approval. A small source/risk spot-check packet is prepared, not
completed clinical validation. The reported prior doctor's source-review scope still
needs a dated record. No current DGDA concordance or national completeness is established.

The prescription image corpus is not deposited. Authors report public MedicalImage
Roboflow material and friend/family contributions consented for research, not image
redistribution. The supplied author/institution decision permits release of derived
detector weights; this statement is recorded without inventing an ethics-committee
approval number. Images, private exports and original notebook outputs remain excluded.
The model card distinguishes author-reported workspace version 2 from directly inspected
artifact metadata and records the remaining historical dataset-link limitations.

A licensed clinician reviewed all 30 navigation fixtures case by case, correcting two
Bengali red-flag presentations to emergency; the rules were extended to match. Every
decision is recorded.
